title: Topological Altermagnetic Insulators
authors: Jasmin Bedow, Nitin Kaushal, Marcel Franz
abstract: We study the emergence of altermagnetic topological phases stabilized by Ising spin-orbit coupling in a prototypical Lieb lattice model of a correlated altermagnet. Treating the electron interactions within the Hartree-Fock and the exact diagonalization techniques, we establish the co-existence of a quantum spin Hall effect with altermagnetic spin order over a wide region of the parameter space for average electron densities of 2 and 4 per unit cell. We explore how the magnetic structure along edges influences the electronic behavior of the associated topological edge modes, demonstrating their robustness against inversion-symmetry breaking terms.
summary: This work theoretically investigates topological altermagnetic insulators modeled on a Lieb lattice. Using Hartree-Fock and ED methods, the authors demonstrate that these correlated systems exhibit coexisting QSHE and altermagnetism. A key focus is analyzing how edge terminations dictate the robustness of helical edge modes against symmetry breaking perturbations.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence and robustness of topological altermagnetic phases stabilized by Ising spin-orbit coupling in correlated electron systems.
main_result: The authors establish that a quantum spin Hall effect can coexist with altermagnetic spin order over wide parameter regions, and they analyze how edge terminations affect the robustness of helical edge modes against symmetry breaking terms like Rashba SOC.
method: Theoretical calculations utilizing Hartree-Fock theory to map phase diagrams, complemented by Exact Diagonalization (ED) techniques for validation on small clusters, and low-energy effective edge theory.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a prototypical Lieb lattice Hamiltonian incorporating hopping terms, local repulsion (Hubbard $U$), and an Ising spin-orbit coupling term ($H_{\lambda I}$).
key_observables: Spin Chern number ($C_s$), staggered magnetization ($	ilde{m}_s$), spectral function of edge modes ($A(k_\parallel, \omega)$), and bond current correlations ($I_{	ext{Bond}}$).
important_parameters: Electron densities (2 and 4 per unit cell), Hubbard interaction strength ($U$), Ising SOC strength ($\lambda_I$), and Rashba SOC strength ($\lambda_{R}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field Hartree-Fock theory, which is later confirmed against quantum fluctuations using ED.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectral function of edge modes for different terminations (Fig. 3), and show the dependence of staggered magnetization and current correlations on $U$ and Rashba SOC strength (Figs. 4 and 5).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the coexistence of topological phases and altermagnetism using HF theory, then develops a low-energy effective edge theory to test robustness against symmetry breaking terms like Rashba SOC, confirming results with ED simulations.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the study of topological protection and gap closing mechanisms under external perturbations (like Rashba SOC) shares conceptual overlap with understanding engineered quantum states in AMO systems.
